chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: Edge video object detection faces high energy costs due to repeated detector invocations on temporally redundant frames. Naive frame-skipping (e.g., FixedSkip-2) causes severe accuracy loss (8.6 pp AP@50 drop) by skipping during critical events like object entry or motion. Existing adaptive methods are insufficient: they require detector retraining, depend on codecs, or fail under ego-motion. ALBIREO fills this gap by enabling detector-agnostic, codec-free, content-aware skipping using per-object temporal state.
chk_problem.reason: The poster accurately describes the research problem as high energy consumption and sustained GPU utilization due to repeated detector invocations on redundant frames, aligning with the reference.

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: ALBIREO wraps off-the-shelf detectors with three mechanisms: 1) Forward-looking uncertainty trigger: Uses 10D Kalman filter per object; skips detection when predicted covariance trace is below threshold u, avoiding stale comparisons. 2) Detector-flicker rescue: On inference frames, emits Kalman-predicted boxes for unmatched confirmed objects if recent confidence was high and rescue cap not exceeded, preventing output fragmentation. 3) Empty-scene screen: Uses lightweight ERD classifier to skip full detection on objectless frames. No detector modification or retraining needed.
chk_method.reason: The poster provides a detailed description of the ALBIREO framework, including its mechanisms (Kalman filter uncertainty trigger, detector-flicker rescue, and empty-scene screen), matching the reference.
